content.text:
<challenge>
Create an unforgettable landing page for a fictional premium brand called **Elysian**.

Use these four images to shape the visual world of the experience:

- https://code.melvynx.dev/elysian-classical-surreal-still-life.png
- https://codelynx.mlvcdn.com/uploads/2026-07-13/2026-07-13-greco-roman-scholarly-landscape.png
- https://codelynx.mlvcdn.com/uploads/2026-07-13/2026-07-13-vibrant-mountain-river-valley.png
- https://codelynx.mlvcdn.com/uploads/2026-07-13/2026-07-13-golden-temple-starry-night.png

The experience should feel imaginative, editorial, luxurious, and slightly surreal. It should make a strong impression immediately and reveal more personality through interaction and movement.
</challenge>

<creative-freedom>
Always prioritize creativity. Make bold, unexpected decisions and develop an original concept rather than following familiar landing-page conventions.

You have complete creative freedom over the story, copy, layout, typography, colors, transitions, and interactions. Use the images in whatever way creates the strongest experience: crop them, layer them, sequence them, transform them, or make them part of the interaction.

Do not place the images into ordinary rectangular sections and call the page finished. Treat them as raw material for a coherent visual world. Avoid generic startup layouts and generic component-library aesthetics.
</creative-freedom>

<delivery>
Build the complete experience in the current repository. It must work beautifully on desktop and mobile.

Do not explain the design before building it. Make the creative decisions yourself and deliver the most original, polished result you can.
</delivery>

Work only inside the current working directory. Do not read, list, search, or edit files outside the current working directory. Treat it as a standalone project root.

Use pnpm exclusively if dependency installation or package scripts are needed. Do not use npm.
Set the browser title and the primary visible title to your model name, using only identity information already available to you. Add nothing else to either title.
Run the relevant checks yourself. Do not edit files outside the current working directory.

content.text:
The Elysian landing page is finished. `pnpm build` passes cleanly, and both the browser `<title>` and the visible `<h1>` say "Claude Opus 5.5" and nothing else. Earlier Playwright runs on desktop and mobile layouts logged no console errors.

The concept is Elysian as a private house of paradise you reach through a sequence of rooms ("cantos"). Each room works one of the four images differently:

- **Opening doors:** The page loads behind a pair of temple doors that swing open onto the hero.
- **Hero:** A WebGL shader shows the still-life as a monochrome copperplate engraving. Moving the cursor burns through it like a lantern, revealing the true colours under a glowing saffron edge. Scrolling burns the whole image into colour, and a closing line fades in on a dark blurred backdrop.
- **Passage:** A long pinned scroll walks you through three nested arched doorways: the Academy, then the Valley, then the Temple. The camera zooms through each arch and finally dives into the temple door, with blur and darkness building so the deep zoom never shows pixelation.
- **Cabinet of Fragments:** The still-life becomes a museum display case. Clickable hotspots stay in sync with catalogue cards and a ledger table, and a magnifying loupe follows the mouse, even while you scroll.
- **The Oracle:** A fanned 3D card deck that tilts and catches light on hover. You draw a card and it flips over to reveal a randomly generated prophecy.
- **Starlit Gate:** The temple image sits under a canvas starfield with twinkling and shooting stars, and constellation lines that follow the cursor. The invitation form is submitted by pressing a wax seal.

It's built with Vite and plain TypeScript, a custom WebGL shader, and Lenis for smooth scrolling. The fonts are Bodoni Moda and EB Garamond. The source images are converted to WebP at several sizes by `scripts/optimize-images.mjs`. The main code is in `src/` (`hero-gl.ts`, `passage.ts`, `cabinet.ts`, `oracle.ts`, `gate.ts`).

To run it: `pnpm dev`, or `pnpm build && pnpm preview`. `scripts/shots.mjs` re-runs the screenshot checks at desktop and mobile sizes.
